title: Welcome, founder.
body: This week you'll find one problem worth solving. Today: notice one thing that annoyed you in the last 24 hours. Write it in your Idea Journal.

title: Problems > Ideas
body: Most failed startups started with an idea looking for a problem. Real founders start with a problem looking for a solution. What's bothering people around you?

title: Eavesdrop today
body: Listen — really listen — to what people complain about at home or school. Write down 3 complaints by tonight.

title: Sridhar's village
body: Sridhar Vembu built a billion-dollar tech company from a Tamil Nadu village. Your starting point isn't your ceiling.

title: Worksheet check-in
body: Open Week 1's 'My Problem List' worksheet. Add one new problem you noticed this week. 60 seconds.

title: Pick one
body: From your list, pick the ONE problem that bothers you the most. Trust your gut. We'll dig into it next week.

title: Week 1 wrap
body: End of Week 1. Take this week's quiz when you're ready — it's not a test, it's a checkpoint.

title: Week 2: Why?
body: This week is about WHY. Every real problem has 5 layers. Today: write your chosen problem in your journal.

title: Five WHYs
body: Ask 'why does that bother me?' five times in a row. Each answer becomes the next question. Try it on yesterday's problem.

title: Falguni @ 50
body: Falguni Nayar started Nykaa at 50. Whatever age you are right now, it is the perfect age to ask one more why.

title: Interview a real person
body: Find one person who has the problem you picked. Ask them ONE 'why' today. Save what they said in your journal.

title: Look for the gap
body: Between 'what people say they want' and 'what they actually do' is where good ideas live. Watch a friend this week.

title: Avoid the trap
body: Don't fall in love with your idea. Fall in love with the problem. Ideas change; the problem stays.

title: Week 2 wrap
body: Take Week 2's quiz. Then rest. Founder weeks are long.

title: Week 3: Who?
body: Now we find the people. Who has your problem most badly? Be specific. 'Everyone' is the wrong answer.

title: Ritesh @ 17
body: Ritesh Agarwal started OYO at 17. He noticed budget hotels were terrible — and he was specifically a young, broke traveller. Specific beats vague.

title: Who pays?
body: The person with the problem isn't always the one with the money. Parents pay for kids' toys. Bosses pay for office software. Who pays for your idea?

title: Customer profile
body: Write a 4-line description of your most likely customer. Age, location, ₹ income, daily routine. Be specific enough that you could spot them in a crowd.

title: Score your idea
body: Use this week's scorecard to rate your idea. Honesty > comfort. A 6/10 you fix is better than a 9/10 fantasy.

title: Pitch to one person
body: Tell one real person your idea in 60 seconds. Write their first reaction. Their face is your first data point.

title: Week 3 wrap
body: Take Week 3's quiz. Most founders skip the customer step. You didn't.

title: Week 4: Story
body: Last week. This week we turn what you learned into a story you can tell — a pitch. A pitch is a story with a number at the end.

title: Failures matter
body: Visit the Failure Museum lessons. Six Indian startups that didn't make it. Each one teaches one rule you don't want to learn the hard way.

title: Pitch Coach today
body: Open the AI Pitch Coach. Record your 60-second pitch. Listen to the feedback. It's free, it's private, and it gets you ready.

title: Money basics
body: Quick bonus: read about Udyam, GST, and the separate bank account. 9 minutes total. Future-you will thank present-you.

title: Idea Journal review
body: Scroll through your Idea Journal. Star the 3 entries that surprise you most. These are your real ideas.

title: Pitch deck PDF
body: Download 'My Pitch Deck' PDF from your Idea Journal. Print it. Show it to one adult who isn't your parent.

title: You did it.
body: Final quiz, then the certificate is yours. Founders ship. You shipped.
